messages:
maya: Heads-up — ACME seeing a big throughput drop on their Dedicated pool rp-ded-42 since ~20:10 UTC. Customers hitting 429s and 300–600ms tail latency. Autoscale didn’t add nodes. Ticket #CS-8421.
ravi: Can you paste a link to the ticket and a few example request IDs? need traces to correlate.
maya: https://support.redwood/acme/CS-8421 ; sample reqs: rqid=acme-8671, acme-8672. Also seeing this alert from metrics-bot.
metrics-bot: ALERT rp-ded-42 high_throttle_rate rate=12% window=5m
josh: Quick ask — did continuous_batcher queue depth spike? packing look bad? any change to max_batch_tokens or scheduler quantum recently?
maya: Pasted recent metrics snapshot:
```
continuous_batcher.queue_depth=118
scheduler.pending_tokens=472000
max_batch_tokens=2048
avg_batch_size=2.1
avg_tokens_per_request=12
```
olivia: avg_batch_size 2.1 is tiny — lots of short prompts. That’ll kill throughput because we’re sending many undersized microbatches. Could be rate pattern + tight scheduler quantum.
ravi: Customer says they send many 5–20 token prompts at ~200 rps during business hours. Tenant id cust-acme-12 accounts for ~92% of traffic in that window.
maya: Support reproduced locally with a loadgen script. Repro steps shared by support team:
```
# simulate short prompts flood
wrk -t8 -c200 -d60s -s scripts/llm-short.lua http://dedicated.redwood/api/v1/generate 
# loadgen lua uses prompt length ~10 tokens, arrival poisson
```
josh: Hypothesis: inefficient token packing + low avg batch size + autoscaler capped at customer commit. Autoscaler logs?
maya: autoscaler log snippet:
```
autoscaler: desired_nodes=8 cap=8 reason="hit_customer_commit_limit"
scale_action: suppressed
```
olivia: If autoscaler hit the customer commit cap we won’t add nodes even if queue backs up. That explains no autoscale. Immediate mitigations: tune scheduler quantum up (more packing latency allowed), bump max_batch_tokens, and apply tenant QoS weight for cust-acme-12.
ravi: Which knobs worked in canary when you tested them?
maya: We did a quick canary on a copied pool: increased scheduler.quantum from 2ms -> 8ms, max_batch_tokens 2048 -> 4096, min_batch_size=4. Results: avg_batch_size rose from 2.1 -> 5.6, throughput +28%, queue_depth down to ~30.
josh: Nice. Also consider enabling rate-aware pack_policy and prefix KV caching if most requests share short prefixes.
olivia: Short-term ops plan: (1) bump scheduler.quantum to 8ms on rp-ded-42 for 10m (2) bump max_batch_tokens to 4096 as canary (3) apply tenant QOS weight 0.5 to cust-acme-12 to avoid noisy neighbor dominance (4) offer customer temporary burst capacity or notify about commit cap.
ravi: Can oncall make the change? Need owner and rollback plan.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: cluster-config-update queued for pool rp-ded-42. Change set: scheduler.quantum=8ms, max_batch_tokens=4096. Rolling restart required. Live-apply flag: true.
josh: Add a guard: track avg_batch_size and throttle rate; rollback if tail latency > 800ms or 5xx increase.
maya: We also proposed policy change to prevent single-tenant floods from starving others: default tenant-fairness weight + automated tenant isolation when avg_batch_size < 3 AND tenant_share > 0.6.
ravi: I'll update the CS ticket with mitigation steps and ask ACME if they can move to batched requests client-side (or accept a small extra latency for better packing).
maya: Summary: root cause = tiny-request flood from single tenant causing inefficient batching and token packing; autoscaler suppressed by customer commit cap. Immediate fixes = scheduler quantum bump, max_batch_tokens bump, tenant QoS. Long-term = autoscale alerting on cap hits + tenant isolation policy + docs for customers on batching best-practices.
olivia: Follow-up: schedule 30-minute postmortem and a short RFC for tenant isolation tuning. tagging paging-oncall for verification :thumbsup:"
